title: Rock cycle
examples: What is the difference between igneous and sedimentary rocks?
Can you explain how heat changes a rock?
What are the main stages in the rock cycle?

explain.say: Today we explore the rock cycle. It shows how rocks change over time. We will look at three main types of rock.
Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: the rock cycle. Look at the magma, the igneous rock and the sediment. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
Igneous rocks form from cooled magma or lava. Magma is rock melted deep underground. Lava is when magma reaches the surface.
Sedimentary rocks form from layers of sediment. Sediment comes from weathered bits of other rocks. These bits are often cemented together.
Metamorphic rocks change due to intense heat and pressure. This changes the original rock's structure. The rock itself does not melt.

draw.text: Metamorphic: Heat and pressure change rock

explain.say: Weathering breaks down exposed rocks into smaller pieces. Erosion moves these pieces away, often by water or wind. This starts the cycle again.
Imagine a river carrying gravel and sand. The sand settles in a lake, forming layers over millions of years. This creates sedimentary rock.

items: Millions of years | Deposition | Layered rock

faq.q: How do rocks change from one type to another?
faq.a: Rocks change through processes like melting, cooling, and being squeezed. These processes are what drive the entire rock cycle.
asks: Can rocks change their type naturally?

faq.q: Is the rock cycle always moving?
faq.a: Yes, the rock cycle is continuous. It shows that no rock type is permanent; they are constantly changing forms.
asks: Does the rock cycle ever stop?
Is the rock cycle a loop?

faq.q: What is the difference between magma and lava?
faq.a: Magma is molten rock found beneath the Earth's surface. Lava is that same molten rock once it has reached the surface.
asks: What happens when magma reaches the surface?

faq.q: Does pressure always make rocks change?
faq.a: Pressure, combined with heat, is what causes metamorphosis. The squeezing action alters the rock's mineral structure.
asks: What is needed for a rock to become metamorphic?
Is heat enough to change a rock?

faq.a: Weathering is the process where rocks are broken down by forces like water or ice. It happens on the Earth's surface.
asks: Is weathering the same as erosion?

facts: Igneous rocks cool from magma or lava.
Sedimentary rocks are formed from layers of sediment.
Metamorphic rocks are changed by heat and pressure.
Weathering breaks rocks into smaller pieces.

quiz.say: A rock cooled slowly deep underground is most likely:
quiz.why: Slow cooling underground allows large, visible crystals to form, which is characteristic of igneous rock.

wrong.0: Sedimentary rocks form from layers of bits, not slow cooling.
wrong.1: Metamorphic rocks are changed by heat, not just slow cooling.
wrong.2: You must choose the single best description for the cooling process.

quiz.say: If a rock is squeezed by deep earth forces, it becomes:
quiz.why: The definition of metamorphic rock involves intense heat and pressure changing its structure.

wrong.0: Sedimentary rocks build up in layers, not by intense pressure alone.
wrong.1: Weathering is the breaking down, not the deep changing by pressure.
wrong.3: Igneous rocks form from cooling magma, not squeezing.

quiz.say: What process creates rock layers from deposited material?
quiz.why: Sedimentation is the process of material settling out of a fluid and forming layers.

wrong.0: Crystallization is more related to cooling magma to form igneous rock.
wrong.1: Subduction is a plate boundary process, not the main layering mechanism.
wrong.2: Metamorphism requires heat and pressure, not just settling layers.
